# Requirements Quality Checklist: Approvals that carry a decision, guided pipeline repair, and a uniform question standard

**Purpose**: Validate that this feature's requirements are complete, clear, consistent and objectively verifiable before planning commits to an approach
**Created**: 2026-09-05
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Review result — 2026-09-05

**45 of 45 satisfied.** Reached in two passes, and the record of both is kept because the first pass is what produced the second.

| Pass   | Result           | What it did                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------ | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Review | 2 → **12 / 45**  | Evaluated all 43 unevaluated items against the specification. 10 satisfied, 33 recorded open with a written statement of what was missing in each.                 |
| Close  | 12 → **45 / 45** | Amended 18 existing requirements, added 13 new ones (FR-037 – FR-049) and 3 criteria (SC-013 – SC-015), and implemented the behaviour the new requirements demand. |

Every item carries both: the `**Open**:` line the review wrote, and the `**Closed**:` line naming what closed it. The open lines are kept rather than overwritten — a checklist that shows only its final state cannot tell a later reader what was actually wrong.

### How the 33 closed

| Route                                 | Count | Notes                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Existing requirement amended          | 18    | The substance already existed elsewhere; the requirement did not point at it                                           |
| New requirement **and** new behaviour | 12    | FR-038 – FR-049. Skills changed: `ccd-pipeline-fix` (7), `ccd-speckit-run` (3), `.claude/rules/repository-docs.md` (2) |
| Closed as unvalidated                 | 1     | CHK038 — FR-037 records the assumption as unvalidated rather than asserting it                                         |
| Closed as moot                        | 1     | CHK044 — FR-027's withdrawal means no multi-document pass can be interrupted                                           |
| Spec gap, not behaviour gap           | 1     | CHK031 — the skill already handled it; the requirement now matches what ships                                          |

### Three worth reading

- **CHK026** found a real mismatch. FR-032 covered feature 006's requirements _"that mandate an approval before every phase"_, but the Supersession record also superseded 006 FR-013, which governs what a proposal _states_. FR-032 now names it explicitly.
- **CHK023 exposed missing behaviour, not missing prose.** FR-016 requires offering a return to diagnosis when validation fails; `ccd-pipeline-fix` had no such return — it dispatched and stopped. Step 5 now implements the loop-back, and FR-039 requires every later cycle to re-obtain both approvals rather than reusing the ones whose evidence turned out not to support them.
- **CHK042 reached an invariant.** An approval given before an interruption was implicitly still held on resume. FR-048 and the `gates` field's `approved` flag — written when the step completes, not when the approval is given — close that. Without it, a resumed run could execute an irreversible step approved against a repository that no longer existed.

### Who did this, and the caveat that still stands

Both passes were run by Claude Code at the maintainer's explicit request, which is the condition `speckit-checklist` permits agent evaluation under. **The same agent drafted most of the specification, evaluated it, and then closed the gaps it found.** That is three roles that would normally be held by at least two people. Each `[x]` names the specific text that satisfies it so any of them can be overturned in one lookup, and the review pass's `**Open**:` lines survive as the record of what a reader was told before the closing pass ran.

## Requirement Clarity — terms that carry the decision

- [x] CHK001 Is "readily undone" defined normatively rather than only in Assumptions, given FR-002 and FR-003 both turn on it? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002] **Open**: defined only under Assumptions — "undone by the maintainer without recovering data or contacting a remote service" — and Assumptions is not normative text. FR-002 enumerates the always-gate set, which covers the practical cases, and `contracts/gate-decision.md` fixes it; neither is a definition inside the requirements. **Closed 2026-09-05**: FR-002 now defines it normatively — reversible by the maintainer alone, in the working tree, without recovering deleted data and without an action by a remote service or another person — and states that the enumerated list is what the definition yields, not a substitute for it.
- [x] CHK002 Is "differs in any way from what the maintainer approved in the plan" specified precisely enough to decide a borderline case — reworded but equivalent, reordered, or a differing artifact list? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-001] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes. FR-001 says "differs **in any way**", which decides every borderline the item lists by making all of them gate — reworded-but-equivalent, reordered, and a differing artifact list each differ, so each asks. A broad rule, but a decidable one.
- [x] CHK003 Is "the plan" the maintainer approved identified as a specific named artifact, so that FR-001's comparison has two defined sides? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001] **Open**: "the plan" is never named as an artifact. FR-006 requires every phase's argument drafted before the first phase runs, which is the thing FR-001 compares against, but no requirement says so — FR-001's comparison has one defined side. **Closed 2026-09-05**: FR-001 now names it — the set of all eight phase arguments drafted and displayed together before the first phase runs, per FR-006 — so the comparison has two defined sides.
- [x] CHK004 Is "normative" defined, given FR-028, FR-029 and SC-010 all rest on distinguishing normative text from other text? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-028] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes. `research.md` R1 gives six mechanical categories plus "every fenced code block is normative in its entirety", and `.claude/rules/repository-docs.md` § What "normative content" means restates it as governing text. `scripts/compaction-audit.sh` implements it.
- [x] CHK005 Is the boundary between a "deliberate, reviewed revision pass" and "incidental reformatting during unrelated work" stated in decidable terms, given that distinction is the entire content of FR-025? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-025] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes. `.claude/rules/repository-docs.md` § The one exception gives four conditions, all decidable: the change's stated purpose, an audit verdict, no normative content dropped, no section reordered or retitled.
- [x] CHK006 Is "verified fix" defined, or does FR-009 rely on the reader inferring it from the bug-remediation workflow's own vocabulary? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009] **Open**: "verified fix" is nowhere defined. FR-015 names the three records and FR-016 refers to "validation does not show the defect resolved", so the term is inferable from the bug workflow's vocabulary — which is exactly what the item asks about. **Closed 2026-09-05**: FR-009 now defines it — the bug workflow's validation stage has run and recorded a result of verified. A partial or failed result is explicitly not a verified fix.
- [x] CHK007 Is "a cause outside the repository's own content" bounded — does a dependency pinned in the repository but broken upstream fall inside or outside? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-018] **Open**: unbounded. The Edge Cases entry gives three examples — an outage, a credential expiry, a runner fault — and settles no boundary. A dependency pinned in the repository but broken upstream falls in neither the examples nor any stated rule. **Closed 2026-09-05**: FR-018 now states the boundary — whether a change to a file in this repository would fix it — and settles the pinned-dependency case as **inside**, with an instruction to ask where it is genuinely unclear.
- [x] CHK008 Is "no default is defensible" given any criterion, or is FR-023's escape hatch available whenever a recommendation is inconvenient to produce? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-023] **Open**: FR-023 supplies no criterion. "The decision is the maintainer's alone and no default is defensible" is self-referential, so the escape hatch is available whenever a recommendation is inconvenient to produce. **Closed 2026-09-05**: FR-023 now supplies an evidential criterion — no default is defensible only when the workflow holds no fact distinguishing the options — and states that difficulty in choosing is not that criterion.
- [x] CHK009 Are "both forges the toolkit already supports" named in the specification, rather than requiring the reader to consult the codebase to know FR-010's scope? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010] **Open**: neither FR-010 nor the Assumptions entry names GitHub or GitLab. Both say "the two forges the toolkit supports", so FR-010's scope requires reading the codebase. **Closed 2026-09-05**: FR-010 now names GitHub and GitLab.
- [x] CHK010 Is "before it begins" in FR-011c anchored to a specific point, distinguishable from FR-011's "before proposing a cause"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011c] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes, and the two are distinguishable. FR-011c's "before it begins" anchors to the capability's own start; FR-011's anchors to before a cause is proposed, which is later. SC-012 states the same contrast as "before the run begins" versus "partway through".

## Requirement Measurability — can a reviewer check it?

- [x] CHK011 Does FR-027 state how much shortening is required, or would removing one character satisfy it? [Measurability, Spec §FR-027] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes, since `research.md` R2 — at least 15% of non-code, non-frontmatter, non-blank characters, stated normatively in `.claude/rules/repository-docs.md` § The length floor. This item is one of the five that forced R1–R3. FR-027 is separately withdrawn, but the measurability question is answered either way.
- [x] CHK012 Does SC-010's "shorter than its previous version" express the intended outcome, given it is satisfied by a trivial reduction? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-010] **Open**, and narrowly so. R2's floor answers the substance, but **SC-010's own text was never amended to reference it** — read alone, "shorter than its previous version" is still satisfied by removing one character. The fix is one clause in SC-010, not new research. **Closed 2026-09-05**: SC-010 now carries R2's floor — 15% of non-code, non-frontmatter, non-blank characters, or a recorded FR-030 exemption — so it is no longer satisfied by removing one character.
- [x] CHK013 Is there a stated procedure by which FR-029's "establishable by comparison" is carried out, or does it rest on a judgement no procedure produces? [Measurability, Spec §FR-029] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes. `research.md` R3 names the procedure, `scripts/compaction-audit.sh` is it, and `contracts/compaction-audit-cli.md` specifies its invocation, output and verdicts. A reviewer runs a command rather than exercising judgement.
- [x] CHK014 Does SC-001's "strictly fewer than the number of phases" capture the intent, given it is satisfied by removing exactly one approval out of eight? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-001] **Open**: SC-001 is satisfied by 7 approvals out of 8. `contracts/gate-decision.md` fixes the always-gate set at six boundaries, which is the real intent, but SC-001's own threshold does not express it. **Closed 2026-09-05**: SC-001 now requires approvals at exactly the always-gate boundaries and no others, and states that a bare inequality is necessary but not sufficient.
- [x] CHK015 Can SC-002 be evaluated after the fact — is a run required to record, per phase, which condition applied? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002] **Open**: SC-002 claims it is "verifiable by inspecting a completed run's record", but no requirement obliges the run to record, per phase, which condition applied. FR-004 requires announcing a reason in the run's output, which is not the same as a durable record. **Closed 2026-09-05**: new **FR-038** requires a per-phase record of which rule fired. Implemented as the `gates` field in `skills/ccd-speckit-run/reference/run-state.md` and written at every boundary per `SKILL.md`. SC-014 measures it.
- [x] CHK016 Is FR-034's "re-examined and its outcome recorded" verifiable, or could any statement whatsoever satisfy it? [Measurability, Spec §FR-034] **Open**: "re-examined and its outcome recorded" is satisfied by any statement whatsoever. The re-examination did happen and is at `research.md` R9, but FR-034 as written would have accepted a sentence asserting it. **Closed 2026-09-05**: FR-034 now requires the record to state which of two outcomes obtains, name the property the reasoning depends on, and say whether it still holds — so a bare assertion no longer satisfies it.
- [x] CHK017 Is SC-009's "stated in exactly one place" checkable given the standard's wording may legitimately be quoted or referenced elsewhere? [Measurability, Spec §SC-009] **Open**: SC-009's "stated in exactly one place" and "zero restatements" do not distinguish a restatement from a legitimate pointer. The check as run greps for the old sentence, which finds restatements of that wording and nothing else. **Closed 2026-09-05**: SC-009 now distinguishes them — a restatement would still tell a reader what the standard requires if the single home were deleted; a pointer would not. Pointers are unlimited.
- [x] CHK018 Are the "length, structure and formatting limits the repository already places on these documents" enumerated or referenced by location, so FR-031 can be checked? [Completeness, Spec §FR-031] **Open**: FR-031 names no location. The limits exist — `.claude/rules/skill-authoring.md` § The three budgets and `.claude/rules/repository-docs.md` § Markdown mechanics — but the requirement points at neither, so checking it requires knowing where to look. **Closed 2026-09-05**: FR-031 now names both files and the specific budgets in each.
- [x] CHK019 Can SC-007's "makes no source-file change of its own" be established by observation, or only by reading the implementation? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes, by observation. FR-015 guarantees `fix.md` exists and records what the bug workflow changed; any source change in the tree absent from that list is the capability's own. Comparing the two is observation, not implementation reading.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK020 Do User Story 1's acceptance scenario 1 and FR-003 agree? **Resolved 2026-09-05**: they did not. The scenario conditioned auto-proceeding on the phase writing "only specification artifacts", while FR-003 conditions it on FR-001 and FR-002 not applying. FR-003 governs; the scenario was amended to test reversibility instead. [Conflict, Spec §US1, §FR-003]
- [x] CHK021 Does FR-008's skip reporting interact consistently with FR-003 — is announcing a skip a form of the FR-004 announcement, a separate obligation, or an approval point in its own right? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, §FR-004] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes. FR-008's "whether or not an approval was requested for it" makes skip reporting unconditional, which settles it as a separate obligation: FR-004 fires only when proceeding under FR-003, and a skipped phase is not a phase proceeding. Neither is it an approval point.
- [x] CHK022 Is FR-020's "every point at which any of the toolkit's workflows requires a decision" consistent with FR-002's list of steps that always require approval, or do the two overlap without saying so? [Consistency, Spec §FR-020, §FR-002] **Open**: they overlap and neither says so. FR-020 covers every decision point in every workflow; FR-002 names steps that always require approval in one of them. FR-002's steps are a subset of FR-020's points, and no requirement states the relationship. **Closed 2026-09-05**: FR-020 now states the relationship — FR-002's steps are a subset of FR-020's points; FR-002 decides whether they ask, FR-020–FR-023 decide what the question looks like.
- [x] CHK023 Do FR-016 (offer a return to diagnosis, uncapped) and FR-013 (offer alternatives before changing anything) state whether a second cycle re-runs the FR-012 and FR-013 approvals or reuses the first cycle's answers? [Gap, Spec §FR-016] **Open**: FR-016 says the return to diagnosis is offered and uncapped, and says nothing about whether a second cycle re-runs FR-012's root-cause approval and FR-013's choice of approach or reuses the first cycle's answers. **Closed 2026-09-05**: new **FR-039** requires every cycle after the first to re-obtain both approvals. Implemented at `skills/ccd-pipeline-fix/SKILL.md` Step 5, which also implements FR-016's loop-back — the skill previously had no return to diagnosis at all, which this item exposed.
- [x] CHK024 Is FR-014's "MUST NOT edit source files itself" consistent with FR-011b's fallback, in which the maintainer supplies output — does supplied output enter the record the same way retrieved output does? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014, §FR-011b] **Open**: FR-011b requires reporting which case occurred and obtaining the output, and nothing states whether maintainer-supplied evidence enters the record the way retrieved evidence does. FR-015 covers the three records but not the provenance of the evidence in them. **Closed 2026-09-05**: FR-011b now states that supplied evidence enters the record as retrieved evidence does, and that the record says which of the two it was.
- [x] CHK025 Are FR-024 ("recorded once, in a single place") and FR-020–FR-023 consistent about whether individual workflows may restate any part of the standard for local emphasis? [Consistency, Spec §FR-024] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes, consistent and explicit. FR-024 says "recorded once, in a single place ... **rather than restated in each workflow**", which names restatement as the thing forbidden; SC-009 measures it as "zero restatements". FR-020–FR-023 state the standard's content and claim no local home for it.
- [x] CHK026 Do FR-032 and FR-033 together account for every requirement of feature 006 that this feature touches, leaving none silently unaddressed? [Completeness, Spec §FR-032, §FR-033] **Open**, and this is a real mismatch. FR-032 covers 006's requirements "that mandate an approval before every phase", which fits 006 FR-010 and FR-011. But the Supersession record also supersedes **006 FR-013**, which is about what a proposal _states_ — the delta row — not about approval. No requirement accounts for that one, so FR-032 and FR-033 together do leave a superseded requirement unaddressed. **Closed 2026-09-05**: FR-032 now extends explicitly to 006 FR-013, naming it as superseded by FR-001 and FR-004 rather than by FR-001–FR-005, so a requirement that did not fit the category no longer goes unaccounted for. This item found a real mismatch, not an imprecision.

## Requirement Completeness — gaps

- [x] CHK027 Does the specification say when and how a maintainer exercises FR-007's override — before the run starts, at any approval, or both? [Gap, Spec §FR-007] **Open**: FR-007 states the override exists and does not say when or how it is exercised — before the run, at any approval, or both. `research.md` R5 and the `gate_mode` field settle it in the implementation; the requirement does not. **Closed 2026-09-05**: FR-007 now states both — offered once when the plan is presented, before the first phase runs, and holding for the whole run; not re-offered at each approval, and recorded rather than remembered so an interrupted run resumes in the chosen mode.
- [x] CHK028 Does FR-007 state whether the override persists for the whole run or applies to a single phase? [Gap, Spec §FR-007] **Reviewed 2026-09-05**: yes. FR-007's "require an approval before every phase **for a run**" states the scope: the whole run, not a single phase.
- [x] CHK029 Is a minimum number of alternatives specified for FR-013, or would a single "approach" satisfy an offer of "alternatives"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013] **Open**: FR-013 says "stated alternative remediation approaches" with no minimum, so one "approach" would arguably satisfy an offer of alternatives. `skills/ccd-pipeline-fix/SKILL.md` requires at least two; the requirement does not. **Closed 2026-09-05**: FR-013 now requires **at least two**, and requires saying so where only one can genuinely be identified rather than presenting one option as a choice.
- [x] CHK030 Does FR-017 cover the case where the maintainer wants several failing jobs addressed together rather than choosing one? [Coverage, Spec §FR-017] **Open**: FR-017 requires asking which subject to take when several could be, and does not cover a maintainer who wants several failing jobs addressed together. The requirement forces a choice the maintainer may not want to make. **Closed 2026-09-05**: new **FR-040** requires "all of them" to be among the offered choices. Implemented at `skills/ccd-pipeline-fix/SKILL.md` Step 1.
- [x] CHK031 Are requirements defined for what the capability does when the failing evidence is retrieved but empty, truncated, or expired by the forge's retention? [Gap, Edge Case] **Open**: no requirement. Retrieval succeeding but returning empty, truncated, or retention-expired evidence is neither FR-011a's success nor FR-011b's failure, so it falls between them. **Closed 2026-09-05**: new **FR-041** names the case and routes it to FR-011b's fallback. The skill already handled it at Step 1 — this was a spec gap, not a behaviour gap, and the requirement now matches what ships.
- [x] CHK032 Are requirements defined for a pipeline that fails intermittently, where one run's evidence does not establish a cause? [Gap, Edge Case] **Open**: no requirement. An intermittently failing pipeline, where one run's evidence does not establish a cause, is not covered by FR-012's "propose a root cause accompanied by the specific evidence supporting it". **Closed 2026-09-05**: new **FR-042** requires reporting evidence as inconclusive and offering to gather more. Implemented at `skills/ccd-pipeline-fix/SKILL.md` Step 2, with the new `stopped: inconclusive` outcome.
- [x] CHK033 Does the specification state who decides FR-019's "would add or alter a requirement", and at what point in the flow that decision is made? [Gap, Spec §FR-019] **Open**: FR-019 says the capability must report that the work is feature work, and does not say who decides that or at what point in the flow — before the root cause is proposed, or after an approach is chosen. **Closed 2026-09-05**: FR-019 now states that the maintainer decides, at the point the remediation approach is chosen, and forbids the capability classifying the work itself and stopping.
- [x] CHK034 Are requirements defined for the FR-030 case's visibility — where a document is left unshortened, is the reason recorded durably or only reported in passing? [Gap, Spec §FR-030] **Open**: FR-030 says the reason is "reported", which a run satisfies by printing it. Nothing requires it recorded durably. It was recorded in `tasks.md` in practice, by convention rather than by requirement. **Closed 2026-09-05**: new **FR-043** requires the reason and percentage recorded durably in the feature's artifacts. Implemented in `.claude/rules/repository-docs.md` § The length floor.
- [x] CHK035 Does the specification address the Edge Cases entry about a phase auto-proceeding and then failing, with a requirement rather than only a narrative note? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases] **Open**: the Edge Cases entry states the obligation in narrative and no requirement carries it. Nothing in FR-001–FR-008 covers a phase that auto-proceeded and then failed. **Closed 2026-09-05**: new **FR-044** requires the failure report to say the phase was one nobody approved individually, forbids offering the auto-proceed as a reason to continue, and forbids presenting the failure as approved. Implemented at `skills/ccd-speckit-run/SKILL.md`.
- [x] CHK036 Does the specification address the Edge Cases entry about shortening removing non-normative but load-bearing context, with a requirement rather than only a narrative note? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-028] **Open**: same shape. The Edge Cases entry names the risk — losing a non-normative but load-bearing passage — and R1 mitigates it by classifying rationale markers as normative, but no requirement states the obligation. **Closed 2026-09-05**: new **FR-045** requires preserving a passage that explains why an odd-looking rule exists, whether or not it matches a normative pattern, and requires widening the patterns rather than dropping such a passage. Implemented in `.claude/rules/repository-docs.md`.
- [x] CHK037 Are requirements defined for what happens when FR-011a's retrieval succeeds but the maintainer disputes that the retrieved run is the right one? [Coverage, Gap] **Open**: no requirement. FR-011a covers retrieval and FR-017 covers ambiguity between several candidates; neither covers a maintainer disputing an unambiguous retrieval. **Closed 2026-09-05**: new **FR-046** requires letting the maintainer name a different run and re-retrieving. Implemented at `skills/ccd-pipeline-fix/SKILL.md` Step 1, distinguished there from Step 0's ambiguity check.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK038 Is the assumption that the bug-remediation workflow is "fit to receive pipeline defects unchanged" validated anywhere, given FR-014 makes the whole of User Story 2 depend on it? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions] **Open**: stated as an Assumption and validated nowhere. FR-014 makes the whole of User Story 2 depend on it, and this repository cannot exercise it — see CHK040. **Closed 2026-09-05** as unvalidated, which is the only honest close. New **FR-037** records the assumption as unvalidated until a run against a repository with a real failing pipeline validates it. It is not asserted true, and this repository cannot make it so — see CHK040.
- [x] CHK039 Is the assumption that artifact compaction "is already served by tooling the repository has installed" verifiable from the specification, given FR-027a excludes artifacts on that basis? [Assumption, Spec §FR-027a] **Open**: "already served by tooling the repository has installed" names no tooling, so the basis for FR-027a's exclusion is not verifiable from the specification. **Closed 2026-09-05**: FR-027a now names the tooling — Spec Kit's `token-budget` extension and its `speckit.token-budget.compact` command, registered in `.specify/extensions.yml`.
- [x] CHK040 Is the consequence of the assumption that this repository runs no pipeline of its own stated as a requirement — that User Story 2 cannot be verified end to end here — rather than only as an assumption? [Assumption, Traceability] **Open**: stated as an Assumption, and `quickstart.md` § Known limit records the consequence — but as a limit on validation, not as a requirement. Nothing obliges the feature to state that User Story 2 is unverified here. **Closed 2026-09-05**: new **FR-037** states it as a requirement — the limit must be stated wherever this feature's verification is reported, rather than the affected scenarios being reported as passing or omitted.
- [x] CHK041 Does the specification record what happens to this feature's own requirements if the maintainer's forge access is revoked between preflight and retrieval? [Assumption, Edge Case] **Open**: no requirement. FR-011c determines availability before the run begins and FR-011b covers retrieval failing; access revoked _between_ those two points is covered by neither in terms, though FR-011b's "the attempt fails" arguably reaches it. **Closed 2026-09-05**: new **FR-047** requires saying that access changed during the run, not merely that retrieval failed. Implemented at `skills/ccd-pipeline-fix/SKILL.md` Step 1.

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK042 Are recovery requirements defined for a run interrupted between an approval and the step it approved? [Coverage, Recovery, Gap] **Open**: no requirement. FR-005 governs what an approval permits and nothing governs an interruption between an approval and the step it approved. **Closed 2026-09-05**: new **FR-048** states that an approval does not survive an interruption and the step is proposed again. Implemented at `skills/ccd-speckit-run/SKILL.md` and in the `gates` field's `approved` flag, which is written when the step completes rather than when the approval is given. SC-015 measures it.
- [x] CHK043 Are requirements defined for the exception flow in which the bug-remediation workflow invoked by FR-014 itself stops or fails? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Gap] **Open**: no requirement. FR-014 mandates the dispatch and FR-016 covers validation not showing the defect resolved; the bug workflow itself stopping or failing is neither. **Closed 2026-09-05**: new **FR-049** forbids reporting a verified fix when the dispatched workflow stopped, and forbids running its remaining stages here. Implemented at `skills/ccd-pipeline-fix/SKILL.md` Step 5, with the new `stopped: bug-workflow-incomplete` outcome.
- [x] CHK044 Are requirements defined for a shortening pass that is interrupted partway, leaving some documents shortened and others not? [Coverage, Recovery, Gap] **Open**: no requirement, and less pressing since FR-027's withdrawal — no multi-document pass is now mandated. It would return with any future pass covering more than one file. **Closed 2026-09-05** as moot. FR-027's withdrawal means no multi-document compaction pass is mandated, so a pass cannot be interrupted partway. Recorded rather than silently dropped: it returns if any future feature mandates a pass over more than one file.
- [x] CHK045 Is each of the four user stories independently deliverable as claimed, given FR-026 sequences FR-025 ahead of User Story 4 and nothing else states a cross-story order? **Resolved 2026-09-05** by `/speckit-analyze` finding F5: User Story 4 is independently testable but not independently schedulable, and `spec.md` §US4 now carries that caveat explicitly. [Consistency, Spec §US1–US4]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- CHK020 was a genuine conflict between User Story 1's first acceptance scenario and FR-003. It was raised and resolved before planning, on 2026-09-05: FR-003's reversibility test governs, and the scenario was amended to match. It is the one item this checklist's author marked, and it is marked because the conflict it names no longer exists.
- CHK004, CHK005, CHK011, CHK012 and CHK013 all circle the same weakness: the compaction requirements rest on an undefined notion of "normative" and set no threshold for "shortened". These are the requirements most likely to be unsatisfiable as written.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
